problem: Existing one-shot embodied tasks (ObjectNav, EQA, GOAT multi-goal nav) only score final outcomes and ignore the exploration process and long-term episodic memory. Current MLLM agents use memory passively (imitation, snapshot filtering, post-hoc reasoning) rather than actively querying it to guide exploration.
motivation: Lifelong-learning agents must build and reuse episodic memory across long-horizon multi-goal tasks and later answer questions about what they saw. The authors argue MLLMs can actively query memory via tools, but no benchmark jointly evaluates navigation and memory-based QA, and no method trains this active retrieval with RL.
key_idea: Fine-tune an MLLM (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) with GRPO and a multi-task reward (action, frontier, answer, format) so it learns to call a memory-retrieval tool proactively during multi-goal exploration, evaluated on the new LMEE-Bench.
insight: Training only on navigation gives no clear gain (SR 20.59 vs baseline 20.96), whereas adding the memory-retrieval tool and QA supervision lifts LMEE SR to 23.53, SPL to 14.99, and QA Acc to 65.52. Removing the tool-usage scaling penalty or the action-frontier consistency penalty lowers performance (SR 21.32 and 22.43), so RL reward shaping toward tool use matters. Goal-oriented QA acts as a task-progress signal that helps planning.
method: LMEE task/benchmark: multi-goal navigation on HM3DSem scenes followed by memory-based QA (attribute, counting, location, relationship, state; open-ended and multiple-choice). Task instructions generated by Qwen3-235B, QA by Qwen3-VL-235B; 1,982 tasks, 3 difficulty levels.

Memory bank: entries (position, CLIP text feature from an image tagger, CLIP image feature) per step; similarity is a weighted sum of text, image and distance terms (0.3/0.5/0.2), with adaptive-threshold filtering over recent samples.

Memory retrieval tool: the MLLM emits code/query text in a first round; an external Python tool encodes it with CLIP and returns top-3 memories by cosine similarity; single-round tool call, falling back to the first-round response if the call fails.
Policy output: the MLLM outputs a single-step ACTION (forward 0.25 m / turn 30°), a FRONTIER selection (frontier-based exploration from Explore-EQA/3D-Mem), and an ANSWER to a goal-oriented question.

Multi-task reward: r = w_act·r_action·c + w_front·r_frontier·c + w_ans·r_answer + w_fmt·r_format, with weights 0.2/0.2/0.4/0.2, consistency coefficient c=0.5 for inconsistent action–frontier pairs, and scale α=1.2 with tool success versus 0.5/0.6 on tool failure; clipped to [0,1].
GRPO RFT via EasyR1: 160 steps, batch 128, lr 1e-6, KL 0.1, 5 generations, 8×H200 (~60 h); 11,684 training samples; intermediate tool responses are not directly optimized.
RA-Mem baseline: 3D-Mem variant where the MLLM generates its own retrieval queries, without RL.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (RL fine-tuned with GRPO) + CLIP retriever
setting.training_data: 11,684 samples from 1,816 LMEE training tasks (HM3DSem 145 scenes, 8,880 goals) with synthetic LLM/VLM-generated instructions and QA
setting.observation: 3 egocentric RGB views (60° apart, 360×360) plus depth for frontier map building, plus retrieved memory images/text
setting.action_space: low-level forward 0.25 m / turn left-right 30°, plus frontier selection
setting.privileged: none at test time (depth and pose used for the map, YOLOv8x-World detection); training memory inserts goal-related memories forcibly

numbers_note: LMEE-Bench is a new benchmark, so it is labeled other. The main-text table uses a 58-task subset; the full-set numbers are in the supplementary material.
results: On LMEE-Bench (subset) MemoryExplorer gets SR 23.53 / SPL 14.99 / QA Acc 65.52, beating RA-Mem (20.96 / 12.18 / 58.62) and 3D-Mem (16.91 / 6.86 / 41.38). On the GOAT-Bench val-unseen subset it reaches SR 46.40 / SPL 28.03 vs RA-Mem 42.81 / 21.95 and 3D-Mem 37.05 / 20.26. The full-set results show the same ranking.
limitations: Slow MLLM inference (about 10-29 h to evaluate) prevents real-time use.
Absolute SR stays low (about 22-24% on LMEE-Bench), and retrieval errors and MLLM spatial understanding limit navigation and QA; the training data is synthetic and ambiguous in places.
Single-round tool call only; main results use a 35% test subset and the frontier voxel map does not support multi-floor scenes.
